text:
maria: Observing a rise in TLS handshake failures for internal inference traffic in us-west-2 and eu-west-3 since ~14:05 UTC. Error pattern is different from previous kms:Decrypt denies — looks like failures during new session ticket generation and OCSP stapling checks.

oscar: Any logs?

maria: proxy excerpt:
```
2026-06-12T14:06:18Z proxy[ingress-usw]: tls: failed to generate session ticket: kms:GenerateDataKey denied for key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:... (principal=svc-keystore-rotator)
2026-06-12T14:06:19Z proxy[ingress-eu]: ocsp stapling failed: cannot fetch responder: http status 403 (cert=cn=inference-edge)
```

anita: I pulled IAM audit: at 14:03:50 policy-shipper applied a scoped policy that removed kms:GenerateDataKey from keystore roles and added a condition restricting calls to specific service principals. It intended to limit key creation but accidentally prevented the rotator and session-ticket agent from getting data keys.

policy-bot: IAM Audit: PutRolePolicy role=keystore-agent-prod user=infra-ci change=chg-4512 mode=ENFORCING

anita: The keystore flow uses GenerateDataKey to create ephemeral symmetric keys for session tickets. If that call fails, we can't issue new tickets and some clients attempt full handshake and then fail when the cert chain can't be stapled (rotator couldn't fetch OCSP because its cert fetch uses the same keystore principal).

oscar: So not just Decrypt — this is GenerateDataKey + ocsp fetch break. Does the audit stream show who was excluded by the condition?

anita: Yes — policy applied a Condition: StringNotEquals: aws:PrincipalTag/role -> ["keystore-rotator","session-agent"] because of a tagging mismatch in infra. The infra CI intended to exclude non-prod but tag matching failed and production principals were excluded.

rotator: rotation log: attempt to create new session key failed: KMS error: AccessDeniedException: user is not authorized to perform kms:GenerateDataKey on key alias/redwood-session-usw. OCSP fetch failed after rotation attempt; stapling service returned 403.

maria: Impact: new sessions fail to issue tickets; existing tickets still work until expire, but within 12 minutes (typical ticket TTL) a large portion of clients will see degradation. We hit ~9% client 5xx for internal generate endpoints in us-west-2 and ~6% in eu-west-3.

oscar: Mitigations?

anita: Immediate options: 1) revert PutRolePolicy to the previous SHADOW version 2) create a temporary KMS Grant allowing GenerateDataKey for the two principals while we fix tags 3) temporarily route new session creation to a separate regional keystore that still has correct policy.

policy-bot: runbook.action: create-grant -> creating KMS Grant principal=svc-keystore-rotator,svc-session-agent scope=GenerateDataKey resource=alias/redwood-session-usw duration=20m

rotator: After the grant, session key generation resumed in us-west-2 within 90s; ocsp stapling still lagged for eu-west-3 (policy revert pending there).

sre_pager: Creating INC-2026-2033, paging owners. Adding route to avoid nodes that report repeated GenerateDataKey denies.

oscar: Can we add better preflight checks? This one is an awkward tag mismatch combined with a Condition.

anita: Proposed changes: A) policy-shipper must refuse non-shadow keystore policy changes unless a new tag-affinity test passes (owner=infra) B) add a preflight smoke test that calls kms:GenerateDataKey using the target principals in region and asserts success (owner=security) C) make proxy emit structured audit events when ticket-gen or stapling fails: {"event":"session_ticket_gen_failure","region":"us-west-2","kms_request_id":"r-xyz","principal":"svc-keystore-rotator","reason":"KMS:AccessDenied"} D) add an alert on metric tls.session.new_tickets.fail.kms_generate > 1/min.

maria: Also recommend we separate concerns: session-ticket key generation should use a dedicated session-key alias per region with automated grants from the rotator role. That reduces blast radius when keystore role policies change.

oscar: For OCSP stapling, the stapling service should not rely on the same tag-based exclusion logic — it needs an allowlist of principals or a managed grant channel. We should fail rotations rather than publishing partial chains. rotator, can you make rotation fail hard on incomplete chain?

rotator: Yes, I'll change the rotator to abort and notify on partial chain and add a verification step before publishing.

anita: Post-incident actions: 1) policy-shipper guardrail for keystore policies + tag-affinity test (owner=infra) 2) KMS Grant short-lived automation for emergency recoveries with strict approval trail (owner=security) 3) proxy structured audit + metric (owner=maria) 4) rotator must fail on partial chains and emit an alert (owner=rotator) 5) design proposal for region-scoped session-key aliases (owner=oscar).

sre_pager: Confirming traffic normalized in us-west-2 at 14:12 after grant; eu-west-3 normalized at 14:25 after policy revert. Closing the immediate paging but keeping INCIDENT-2026-2033 open for follow-ups.

oscar: One more: add a CI validation that simulates an infra tag drift and verifies policy-shipper behavior — prevents the shadow->enforcing flip in prod from accidental tag mismatches.

maria: Agreed. I'll draft the postmortem and include the suggested metrics/alerts. Thanks all. :ok_hand:
